basis: Malignant tumour arising from peripheral nerve sheath.
Prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis is a marrow myeloproliferative neoplasm.
Corpus callosum agenesis and blepharophimosis define brain and eyelid abnormalities; additional organ damage is not established.
Defining rib, pelvic and limb skeletal dysplasia; narrow chest alone does not establish lung damage, and renal disease is not documented.
Thymic tumour origin falls outside the listed axes; neuroendocrine histology alone establishes neither endocrine gland disease nor immune-mediated disease.
Hereditary erythrocytosis defines blood involvement. Thromboses are separately coded complications; isolated 1/1 reports do not establish population frequency.
Mitochondrial myopathy with defining ophthalmoplegia; hearing impairment 30–79%. Neuropathy, ataxic lesions and cardiomyopathy are mostly 5–29%; respiratory weakness is muscular.
Genetically defined intellectual disability and neurodevelopmental disorder.
Progressive myocardial dystrophy with fibrofatty replacement; skin findings belong to particular syndromic subtypes.
Combined immunodeficiency is defining; TBX1 alone does not establish cardiac, endocrine or other organ abnormalities.
Astrocytic tumour occupying cerebral cortex and leptomeninges; hypotropia alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Malignant occupation of the spleen, covered by the haematologic axis. The umbrella includes non-lymphomatous tumours, so lymphoma mechanism is not universal.
Diphtheria-associated infectious myocardial injury defines the disease.
Broad terminal thumb and great-toe phalanges establish skeletal abnormalities; palpebral slant does not establish ocular damage, and intellectual disability is unspecified.
Disease located in the basal ganglia; vascular or metabolic mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Direct chemical injury and inflammation of the colon; no infectious or immune-mediated mechanism is established.
Obstetric complication of monochorionic pregnancy; fetal circulatory consequences do not establish maternal cardiovascular disease.
Tumour arising in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the listed axes.
Tumour of endocrine pancreatic cells, including functional and nonfunctional subtypes; exocrine pancreatic damage is not defining.
Congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells defines intestinal obstruction, directly affecting the enteric nervous system and bowel.
Postsynaptic transmission disorder with SCN4A-related myopathy and periodic paralysis; ocular and respiratory findings reflect muscle/NMJ weakness.
Defining skeletal embryopathy; intellectual disability 30–79% supports neurologic involvement. Cardiac/ocular defects 5–29%; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct lung injury.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with sperm flagellar abnormalities and infertility; reproductive function has no listed axis.
Caustic oral/GI injury and direct pulmonary toxicity; acute kidney injury roughly 40–70% and hepatic injury around 30–50% in clinically significant poisoning.
Intestinal bacterial colonization produces toxin-mediated NMJ paralysis. Colonization does not establish bowel injury; ocular and respiratory findings arise from neuromuscular blockade.
